notes.b: Water polo is a team ball game played in deep water, so the rules are shaped by the fact that players cannot stand and must keep themselves afloat while they play.
points: Two teams play, each with six field players and a goalkeeper in the water, seven in total.
The aim is to throw the ball into the opponents' goal; the team that scores more goals wins.
Field players may handle the ball with one hand only, because both arms are needed to stay afloat and the one-hand rule keeps play fast; the goalkeeper may use two.
Field players may not touch the bottom of the pool, so they must tread water for the whole game; in some pools the goalkeeper may touch the bottom.
notes.tip: Say seven players per team in the water, including the goalkeeper, and one hand only on the ball for field players.

notes.b: Because players cannot stand, every skill in water polo starts from how they stay up and how they swim. Two movements underpin everything else.
points: Eggbeater kick: an alternating circular leg kick (one leg circles, then the other, like the beaters of a whisk) that keeps the player high and stable in the water.
The eggbeater kick lets the player pass, shoot and defend from a high position, because the legs hold the body up and leave both arms free.
Head-up front crawl: the normal front crawl swimming stroke, but with the head kept up, so the player can see the ball and the other players while swimming.
notes.tip: If asked why the eggbeater kick matters, say it keeps the player high and stable so they can pass, shoot and defend.

notes.b: Passes move the ball between team-mates without anyone touching the bottom. There are two main types, and the difference is whether the ball touches the water.
points: Dry pass: thrown to the receiver's hand above the water, and caught without touching the water, so it is quick and the receiver can shoot at once.
Wet pass: put into the water in front of a team-mate, who swims onto it (swims to meet the ball and collects it).
The passer uses the eggbeater kick to rise out of the water, which gives height and room to throw.
Passes can be made with one hand from above the head, which fits the one-hand rule for field players.
notes.tip: Define both passes by what the ball does: a dry pass goes to the hand above the water, a wet pass goes into the water in front of a team-mate.

notes.b: A goal is scored by throwing the ball past the goalkeeper, so players choose a shot to suit their position in the water and where the goalkeeper is.
points: Power shot: taken from above the head, with an eggbeater lift and body rotation, so the whole body adds force to the throw.
Push shot: taken from the water surface, without needing to rise high out of the water.
Backhand shot: thrown with the back of the throwing hand leading.
Lob: a high shot played over the goalkeeper.
Aim for the corners of the goal, because they are hardest for the goalkeeper to reach.
notes.tip: Describe each shot by where it is taken from or how it travels: above the head, water surface, back of the hand leading, or high over the goalkeeper.

notes.b: A player who has the ball can swim with it rather than pass, a skill called dribbling. It uses the head-up front crawl, so the player can see the field while swimming.
points: Dribbling: the player swims head-up front crawl with the ball between the arms, so the player can still watch the other players.
The ball is pushed forward by the bow wave of the swimmer (the wave of water that builds up in front of the swimming body).
notes.tip: For dribbling, give both the technique (head-up front crawl, ball between the arms) and how the ball moves (pushed forward by the bow wave).

notes.b: Moving free means getting away from your marker (the defender who is guarding you) so a team-mate can pass to you. It is what an attacker does when they do not have the ball.
points: Sprint and change direction to lose a marker, because a defender cannot easily follow a sudden change.
Drive towards the goal, which puts the attacker in a shooting position and forces the defence to react.
Position to receive the ball, so the passer has a clear target.
notes.tip: Cover all three parts: sprinting and changing direction to lose a marker, driving towards goal, and positioning to receive.

notes.b: Defenders mark an opponent (stay close to them) and try to intercept passes (catch or knock away a pass meant for someone else) to stop the attacking team scoring.
points: Stay between the opponent and the goal, so any shot or drive has to get past the defender.
Use the eggbeater kick to stay high in the water, which lets the defender reach and block.
Raise an arm to block passes and shots.
Anticipate passes (read where the ball is going) so the defender can intercept it.
notes.tip: A full answer on marking and intercepting gives all four: position between opponent and goal, eggbeater to stay high, arm raised to block, and anticipating passes.

notes.b: The rules protect players, who are partly hidden under water and easy to hold or pull down, and keep play moving.
points: Field players use one hand only on the ball.
No holding, sinking or pulling an opponent who does not have the ball, because the player without the ball is not allowed to be obstructed.
Such a foul may be an ordinary foul or an exclusion foul (a more serious foul where the offender is sent out of the water for a period).
A shot clock (a timer) limits how long a team may keep possession without shooting, so teams must attack rather than hold the ball.
The pool has a 2 m line and a 5 m line marked out from the goal, and these lines are part of the rules.
notes.tip: Describe the rules in words, such as one hand only, no holding, sinking or pulling, and a shot clock. Do not give shot clock or exclusion times.

notes.b: Teams attack and defend with set roles and plans. Knowing the positions and the options after possession changes is the basis of water polo tactics.
points: The centre forward sets up in the hole set, in front of the goal, which is the main scoring position.
Drivers are field players who attack by driving towards the goal.
After a turnover (when possession changes from one team to the other), a team may counter-attack quickly, before the defence is organised.
Defence is played as zone (each defender covers an area) or man-to-man (each defender marks one opponent).
After an exclusion, the attacking team has an extra player and uses it to create a shot.
notes.tip: Water polo appears in written answers on structures and strategies. Name the position or tactic and say what it is for, such as the centre forward in front of goal or the extra player after an exclusion.

notes.b: Water polo involves contact, fast throws and deep water, so a few precautions reduce the risk of injury.
points: Caps with ear guards protect the ears from the ball and from contact.
Fingernails are trimmed, so players do not scratch one another when they contest the ball.
No jewellery is worn, because it can injure other players or be lost.
Deep water is supervised, so help is at hand if a player is in difficulty.

notes.b: Players tread water, sprint and contest the ball for the whole game, so the game makes several fitness demands.
points: Cardio-respiratory endurance (heart and lungs working for long periods) and muscular endurance: the legs work for long periods in the eggbeater kick.
Power: needed for the shooting skills, which add force through body rotation and lift.
Agility in the water: quick changes of direction when moving free and marking.
Physical contest: close marking and blocking involve physical contact.
notes.tip: In fitness demands answers, link each demand to a skill: endurance to the eggbeater legs, power to shooting, agility to moving free and marking.

keyTerms.definition: An alternating circular leg kick that keeps the player high and stable in the water.
A pass thrown to the receiver's hand above the water, caught without touching the water.
A pass put into the water in front of a team-mate, who swims onto it.
A shot taken from above the head with an eggbeater lift and body rotation.
A high shot played over the goalkeeper.
Moving with the ball by swimming head-up front crawl with the ball between the arms.
The centre forward's position in front of the goal.
A field player who attacks by driving towards the goal.
A quick attack made after possession changes hands, moving the ball upfield.
A serious foul that removes the offending player from the game for a period and gives the opposing team an extra player.
A timer that limits how long a team may keep possession without shooting.
A defence in which each defender marks one opponent.
A defence in which each defender guards an area rather than a single player.

factCards.term: How many players does each team have in the water?
factCards.definition: Six field players and a goalkeeper, seven in total.

factCards.term: How many hands may a field player use on the ball?
factCards.definition: One hand only. The goalkeeper may use two.

factCards.term: Where does a wet pass go?
factCards.definition: Into the water in front of a team-mate, who swims onto it.

factCards.term: How is a power shot made?
factCards.definition: From above the head, with an eggbeater lift and body rotation.

questions.prompt: Explain two skills used in water polo and give key technique points for each.
questions.model: Dry pass: the ball is thrown to the receiver's hand above the water, so it is caught without touching the water. The passer uses the eggbeater kick to rise out of the water and passes with one hand from above the head. Power shot: the shot is taken from above the head, with an eggbeater lift that raises the player out of the water. The player rotates the body and throws the ball, aiming for the corners of the goal.

questions.prompt: Describe the eggbeater kick and explain why it is important in water polo.
questions.model: The eggbeater kick is an alternating circular leg kick, in which the legs move in circles out of step with each other. It keeps the player high and stable in the water. It is important because it leaves the arms free to pass, shoot and block, and without it the player would sink and lose the height needed to pass, shoot or defend.
